Same discipline as data/ws6b_params.json: every figure carries its source, and 'uncertain': true means the pull could NOT confirm it from a published source and it is a stated assumption, NOT a verified figure - such a figure must be reported as uncertain wherever it propagates. Retrieval date for all pulls: 2026-09-19. This file compares WRAPPERS for one exposure (MSCI Emerging Markets), not a fund against its own constituents: direct replication of EM is infeasible and is recorded as such under 'direct_route_rejected'.

source_country_withholding_differential.note: THE ONE MATERIAL GAP. Both funds hold non-US stocks and both suffer withholding in each source country at whatever rate that country's treaty with the fund's domicile allows. Ireland's and the United States' treaty networks over the large MSCI EM weights - Taiwan 25.7%, China 20.3%, South Korea 17.6%, India 12.3% (justETF country weights for IE00B0M63177 as of 2026-07-30) - are NOT the same, and this pull did not establish either. The differential could run in either direction and is deliberately NOT netted into the headline. Closing it needs treaty texts or a specialist, not a product page.

us_estate_tax.note: EEM is us_situs true and an Irish UCITS is not. US estate tax applies to US-situs assets of non-resident aliens above a USD 60,000 exemption, and Singapore has no US estate tax treaty. This is a LARGE asymmetric benefit of the Irish route that is deliberately left unpriced here. The vault already carries a caution that estate-tax figures in the ETF Starter work were not primary-sourced; the same caution applies. Needs counsel.

switching_cost.note: One-off: sell EEM, buy the Irish line, crossing two spreads plus commission, plus any capital gains consequence (none for a SG individual on equities, not verified here) and time out of the market.

holding_vehicle_invariance.asked: 2026-09-20 - would holding through a Cayman SPV make the US-domiciled ETF or the direct stocks more attractive than the Irish UCITS?
holding_vehicle_invariance.answer: NO, and the ranking does not move at all.
holding_vehicle_invariance.reasoning: A holding vehicle changes withholding only if it changes the TREATY that applies. Cayman has no US income tax treaty, so a Cayman entity receiving US-source dividends suffers the same statutory 30% as a Singapore individual - no improvement on the direct-stock or US-ETF route. The Irish UCITS keeps its 15% fund-level rate regardless of who owns it, because a fund's treaty position is the fund's own and not its holders', and Ireland does not withhold on distributions to non-residents (TCA 1997 s739D), so a Cayman holder sits at 0% at investor level just as an SG individual does. Every verdict in this file and in the 2026-09-19 WS6b amendment is driven by the 15%-versus-30% step, which is untouched.

holding_vehicle_invariance.what_a_blocker_does_change: US estate tax only. That applies to US-situs assets of a non-resident INDIVIDUAL; a corporation does not die, so a non-US corporate blocker removes the exposure. It is listed under not_quantified above and was deliberately never netted into any headline, so removing it changes no ranking - it removes a tiebreaker, not a result.
holding_vehicle_invariance.what_a_blocker_adds: Recurring Cayman administration, audit, directors, registered office and economic-substance cost, plus FATCA/CRS obligations. Every figure in this file is 20-100 bps; the fixed cost is five figures a year and must be compared against the TOTAL pool it covers, not one sleeve. SEPARATE RISK, NOT RESOLVED: if the vehicle is managed and controlled from Singapore it may be SG tax-resident, and the s13(9) foreign-sourced income exemption requires a foreign headline rate of at least 15% - Cayman has none - so the structure could be tax-negative. A legal question, flagged not answered.
holding_vehicle_invariance.what_would_change_it: Only a vehicle domiciled somewhere with a better US treaty rate than Ireland's 15%, which for a pooled equity vehicle does not exist at this scale. Ireland is already near the best available.

direct_route_rejected.note: Direct replication of EM constituents is rejected before any tax argument. From the holdings archive: ICHN needs 216 names to reach 90% of fund weight, IJPN 164, NDIA 75, ITWN 53. Norgate carries no non-US equity data, so the basket could be neither backtested nor tracked; the vault already established that Norgate sells no European product at any tier. Several of these markets also gate foreign investors behind registration. No further work proposed.
